topic: FY 2027 DA budget reduction and available fiscal space
summary: The chair and Undersecretary Nora Olivares presented substantial reductions in the agriculture-sector and DA budgets, including a reported agriculture-sector decrease of about 35.3 billion and a DA decrease of about 17.2 billion, or 8%. The presentation also showed the farm-to-market road allocation falling from 33 billion in 2025 to 16 billion in 2027. A minority representative and the chair questioned whether fiscal space constrained priority programs and whether irrigation projects were being selected transparently. DA and NIA officials cited fiscal ceilings, economic viability, project readiness, statutory requirements, geographic disadvantage, drought, and irrigation-development levels as selection criteria. The chair raised 46,000,000 in fiscal space and concerns about anomalous infrastructure insertions, while NIA described technical validation, costing, procurement, audit, engineering, and reporting controls. The agency committed to submit documentation on irrigation projects under Agrarian Reform Fund guidelines, leaving broader restoration and transparency questions open.
question: The committee sought to establish why the FY 2027 DA and agriculture-sector budgets were reduced, how much fiscal space remained for restoration or priority programs, and how DA and NIA would prioritize projects within that constraint. It also sought the basis for NIA irrigation-project selection and documentation to guard against irregular infrastructure insertions.
agency_position: The DA and NIA attributed the proposed reductions to limited fiscal space and budget ceilings, while maintaining that priority programs and projects would be selected through economic, technical, readiness, statutory, geographic, climate, and government-priority criteria. The agencies defended project controls based on validation, costing, procurement and audit rules, engineering requirements, monitoring, and congressional reporting, and agreed to submit material concerning irrigation projects under Agrarian Reform Fund guidelines.
outcome: The DA and NIA explained that fiscal-space limits drove the proposed reductions and described their project-prioritization and control procedures. The issue remained open for congressional review, with the agency committed to submit irrigation-project documentation under Agrarian Reform Fund guidelines.

topic: Farm-to-market-road funding, unit costs, releases, and transparency
summary: Members questioned the proposed 16,000,000,000 FY 2027 FMR budget against an estimated 55,000-kilometer network and a reduction from 33,000,000,000 in 2026. DA said project selection considered farmers, production, poverty, connectivity, road condition, climate, traffic, and new production areas, and identified about 60 billion annually as a bare-minimum ideal that could build about 4,000 kilometers. The minority also challenged unit costs ranging from 9,400,000 to 15,900,000 per kilometer, large Benguet projects, and incomplete or questionable project coordinates. DA attributed the higher 15,000,000 cost to fuel and construction-price increases and promised to check the coordinates and present reports. Members further asked about releases, with the transcript citing 10,700,000,000 as the corrected 2025 release and 5.7 as a current release figure whose meaning was unclear. DA's infrastructure official requested an additional 30,000,000,000 for 2,000 kilometers, and Rufus Rodriguez endorsed tripling the allocation, but no final funding decision was recorded.
question: The committee sought to establish whether the FY 2027 farm-to-market-road allocation was sufficient, how projects and unit costs were selected, and whether DA could implement the program transparently and within available capacity. Members also asked about releases, road standards, project coordinates, regional allocations, and the effect of budget restrictions on implementation.
agency_position: DA said FMR priorities were selected using beneficiary, poverty, production, connectivity, road-condition, climate, traffic, and new-production-area criteria. The department maintained that 16,000,000,000 was insufficient against the network gap, identified about 60,000,000,000 annually as a bare-minimum ideal, and supported additional funding while retaining flexibility to adjust standards and routes based on terrain, production needs, and implementation capacity.
outcome: The agency answered the committee's general questions on prioritization, unit costs, releases, and implementation constraints, but concerns over the FY 2027 reduction, Benguet concentration, coordinates, and DA-DPWH standards remained open. DA undertook to provide or present supporting reports, while NIA agreed to submit a written proposal on implementation flexibility; the request to increase or triple FMR funding was not shown as a final appropriation.

topic: NIA irrigation budget, project prioritization, and district allocations
summary: The chair and NIA administrator presented a FY 2027 irrigation proposal of about 233.85 billion, against an NEP amount of about 47.43 billion, and NIA sought House support for an increase. NIA said the reduced fiscal space required priority for ongoing, validated, high-impact, and implementation-ready projects, while members questioned district allocations, Region 8 funding, Bukidnon support, and the adequacy of maintenance and development funding. The agency described prioritization criteria that included irrigable potential, fiscal and economic viability, project readiness, statutory requirements, geographic disadvantage, and drought exposure. Members Allan Ty and Robert Nazal Jr. pressed NIA on whether program-based appropriations or rigid itemized listings better protected accountability and implementation; NIA preferred program-based appropriations supported by separately submitted project lists. NIA committed to submit allocation and project documents, modification lists, and its request to restore program-based budgeting. The requested budget increase and disputed district allocations remained open for subsequent committee action.
question: The committee sought to establish whether NIA's FY 2027 funding was sufficient to expand, rehabilitate, restore, and climate-proof irrigation systems, and how the agency prioritized projects and district allocations under fiscal constraints. Members also asked whether NIA should retain program-based appropriations or return to rigid, itemized project listings, and what documents and safeguards would preserve congressional oversight.
agency_position: NIA maintained that the FY 2027 allocation was constrained by fiscal space and therefore had to prioritize tier-one, ongoing, validated, high-impact, and implementation-ready projects. It supported restoring program-based appropriations, with detailed project lists submitted separately for DBM validation, congressional oversight, transparency, and reporting, while seeking greater operational flexibility to respond to changed field conditions.
outcome: The agency's funding request and prioritization framework were presented, but the proposed increase and several district and regional allocation complaints were not finally resolved. NIA committed or was asked to submit project lists, allocation breakdowns, modification requests, and a proposal for program-based flexibility, leaving the budget level and specific allocations for further committee consideration.

Irrigation allocations should be distributed equitably toward high-producing districts, and a 5,000,000 maintenance allocation for his district's systems was inadequate.
Region 8's steeply declining allocation required explanation and a province-level breakdown, and NIA needed more flexibility to implement validated projects.
Validated irrigation projects in his district deserved a proportional increase rather than the reported 12,000,000 allocation.
His district's zero allocation was unacceptable because upland areas lacked water and needed solar pumping irrigation.
Bukidnon's high agricultural output warranted continued and adequately documented NIA support.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair stated that the FY 2027 NEP proposed 198,450,000,000 for the DA and attached corporations, and 46,360,000,000 as budgetary support for NIA.

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair said the NEP proposed 46,360,000,000 in budgetary support for NIA, while only 2,200,000 hectares had been developed out of a potential irrigable area of 3,130,000 hectares. The committee expected irrigation projects to be coordinated with commodity plans, crop calendars, LGUs, and irrigators' associations.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: The administrator said NIA's FY 2027 proposal aimed to accelerate new irrigation development, rehabilitate and restore existing facilities, expand climate-resilient technologies, and strengthen nationwide irrigation reliability. He said the proposal was anchored on NIA's seven-point strategic agenda and the National Irrigation Master Plan for 2020 to 2030.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: The administrator said the updated methodology expanded the slope criterion from 3% to up to 8%, increasing the estimated net potential irrigable area by more than 4,000,000 hectares. In some regions, suitable areas could have slopes up to 45% where solar-powered pump and other technologies could be adapted.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: As of 12/31/2025, NIA had developed 2,200,000 hectares out of an estimated potential of 3,130,000 hectares, or 70 per point 25% of the country's irrigation potential. The administrator said around 1,000,000 hectares, approximately 30%, remained to be developed, and 1,790,000 hectares, or 82%, of the developed area were under NIA-assisted systems.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: NIA proposed a total FY 2027 budget of 233,850,000,000 pesos, but the FY 2027 NEP provided only 47,430,000,000. The administrator said this was below the 2026 budget of 64 65,000,000,000 and required prioritization of implementation-ready, high-impact projects.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: For operations, NIA proposed 211,010,000,000, but only 30,440,000,000 was included in the NEP. The administrator said this was 39% lower than the FY 2026 GAA and would significantly limit nationwide irrigation implementation.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: NIA proposed 219,000,000,000 for capital outlay, but only 33,000,000,000 was included in the NEP. The administrator identified the capital-outlay reduction as the principal constraint because capital outlay comprised most of NIA's irrigation investment requirements.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: For irrigation-system restoration, NIA proposed 5,950,000,000 for climate-change adaptation works, including 223,000,000 for national irrigation systems and 473,000,000 for communal irrigation systems and watershed-management areas. For service-road improvement, NIA proposed 17,710,000,000 for national systems and 2,390,000,000 for communal systems, but only 250,000,000 was included.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: For repair, NIA proposed 38,260,000,000 for national irrigation systems, 20,520,000,000 for communal systems, and 10,420,000,000 for pump systems, or around 70,000,000,000. The FY 2027 budget provided only 2,920,000,000 and 3,000,000,000 respectively, as spoken.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: For new irrigation development, NIA proposed 34,940,000,000 for new national irrigation-system projects and 11,800,000,000 for small reservoir projects, while the FY 2027 budget provided 7,560,000,000 and 4,580,000,000 respectively. Proposed priority projects included the Halor River multipurpose project, Balog-Balog multipurpose project phase two, Ilocos Norte–Ilocos Sur–Abra irrigation projects, and the Tomahweeny Reveal Multiple Post Project, with names partly unclear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: The NEP included 7,920,000,000 for pump irrigation projects, 4,580,000,000 for special irrigation projects, 200,000,000 for extension and expansion, and 698,000,000 for CARB IC. NIA projected 4,160 hectares of new irrigated areas and restoration of 531 hectares.

thread.speaker: NIA Administrator Eduardo Guillén
thread.said: NIA formally sought House support for an increase in its FY 2027 budget, saying additional funding was essential to accelerate development, restore and rehabilitate systems, deploy climate-resilient technologies, and support food security.

thread.speaker: Rep. Ian Amatong
thread.said: Amatong questioned why his district had received zero allocations in earlier years and only 7,000,000 this year, asking for an explanation of the allocation method. He emphasized that his district had extensive irrigable land and poverty-related needs.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: The NIA official said the agency had requested almost 250,000,000,000 but faced fiscal limitations, with only 46,000,000,000 available as stated in the exchange. Available funds were directed to operations, personal services, operation and maintenance, pump irrigation, contractual obligations, and ongoing national irrigation projects.

thread.speaker: Rep. Ian Amatong
thread.said: Amatong said his district had received only 7,000,000 despite having the largest irrigable land area in the region. The agency cited location and allocation considerations, including 47,000,000,000 for the central office and 16,000,000,000, with one-third allocated to districts, as spoken.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: The official said the total proposed district budget was 790,000,000 and that the available amount would focus on ongoing projects. The official invoked Congress's power of the purse and said priority would be given to tier-one and continuing projects.

thread.speaker: Rep. Ian Amatong
thread.said: Amatong asked that the budget discussion be deferred so the deputy administrator for engineering and technical matters could address the district and project concerns. The chair then suspended the hearing.

thread.speaker: Minority representative Kaka Bag-ao
thread.said: Bag-ao asked for the total FY 2027 irrigation budget, including special irrigation projects and other NIA programs, and requested a consolidated project and amount breakdown. She linked the request to drought and El Niño conditions and the need to address the remaining 30% of irrigation potential.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: The agency said that its El Niño response included development, repair, and installation of solar-powered irrigation systems, and that NIA would explain the 30% remaining area and provide the breakdown. When pressed for the specific FY 2027 amount, the official said the data would have to be checked.

thread.speaker: Minority representative Kaka Bag-ao
thread.said: Bag-ao requested that the documents and intervention breakdown be submitted to her, preferably during the hearing, to support proposed budget increases and oversight.

thread.speaker: NIA project planning division manager Raul Mark Reveliamepo
thread.said: Reveliamepo explained that project prioritization used weighted criteria, including contribution to irrigation development, regional irrigation master plans, fiscal space, economic viability, stage of development, government priorities, statutory requirements, and whether an area was geographically isolated and disadvantaged. Drought incidence had recently been added to the prioritization process.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA said projects underwent technical validation, prioritization, costing, implementation-readiness assessment, DBM evaluation, procurement and auditing requirements, engineering and environmental review, and monitoring and reporting to Congress. The agency emphasized the standard of 'right project, right price, right quality.'

thread.speaker: Committee chair
thread.said: The chair asked whether NIA would submit the irrigation projects under Agrarian Reform Fund guidelines. The agency answered, 'Yes,' and committed to submit them.

thread.speaker: Rep. Allan Ty
thread.said: Ty asked how NIA received, appropriated, and used national government subsidies, and whether its budget had historically been presented by program expenditure rather than as an extensive list of individual projects.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA confirmed that earlier budgets were generally presented under program and subprogram expenditures, while detailed project lists were submitted as supporting documents. Individual projects were generally not separate line items in the NEP or GAA annex.

thread.speaker: Rep. Allan Ty
thread.said: Ty asked whether NIA still submitted project lists and supporting documents to DBM for technical evaluation, validation, costing, and budget review under the program-based framework.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA confirmed that it submitted project lists and supporting documents to DBM even under program-based budgeting. It said the absence of individual GAA line items did not mean projects were unvalidated or that NIA had unlimited discretion.

thread.speaker: Rep. Allan Ty
thread.said: Ty asked whether program-based appropriations remained subject to DBM evaluation, procurement laws, auditing rules, engineering standards, environmental requirements, monitoring, reporting to Congress, and congressional oversight.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA agreed that program-based budgeting did not remove accountability. It described the requested flexibility as operational flexibility to respond to field conditions, not discretion without accountability, and said the agency had written the Speaker seeking greater flexibility.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA said the FY 2026 practice of making individual projects separate budget line items created significant operational difficulties. Changes in engineering scope, cost, right-of-way, permits, calamities, or other constraints could make a project infeasible, while rigid line items prevented funds from being readily redirected to another validated and implementation-ready project.

thread.speaker: Rep. Allan Ty
thread.said: Ty asked which structure would better serve farmers: a rigid itemized project list in the GAA or program-based appropriations supported by a separately submitted, validated, and transparent project list.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA preferred restoring the program-based structure. It said this would preserve transparency and accountability while allowing the agency to address delays, use legitimate savings, respond to calamities, prioritize validated projects, and improve obligation and disbursement performance.

thread.speaker: Rep. Allan Ty
thread.said: Ty asked whether NIA had formally requested an amendment restoring program- or subprogram-based appropriations instead of rigid itemized listings.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: The agency answered yes and said the detailed project list would remain a supporting document for transparency, validation, monitoring, and oversight rather than a rigid statutory listing.

thread.speaker: Rep. Allan Ty
thread.said: Ty requested that NIA submit to the committee the request it had sent to the Speaker regarding the proposed budget structure.

thread.speaker: Rep. Solomon Chungalao
thread.said: Chungalao asked NIA to prioritize irrigation support for the preservation and restoration of Ifugao rice terraces and other heritage sites. He said irrigation was essential because the terraces were drying and restoration required reliable water.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: The agency indicated that the heritage-related proposal was under consideration and referred to approval, operational limitations, and the need for facilitation. The response was garbled and did not establish a specific funded commitment.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal asked whether the FY 2026 itemized project structure and special provision number eight had improved implementation or contributed to lower NIA budget utilization. He asked which structure would preserve accountability while providing sufficient implementation flexibility.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA said it preferred program-based operations supported by a detailed, validated, and transparent project list submitted separately to Congress and DBM. It said adjustments would remain within the approved program and comply with budgeting, procurement, auditing, and reporting requirements.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal asked NIA to submit a written proposal on changes to the special provisions before plenary consideration.

thread.speaker: Rep. Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal warned that when Congress substantially reduced a designed and costed irrigation project, the remaining amount might not produce a functional project and could result in an incomplete system. He manifested that implementability should be considered when the House or Senate adjusted project amounts.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez said his district had proposed 125,000,000 for irrigation but received zero in the NEP, including no solar water-pumping irrigation. He said a consultation had consolidated 125,000,000 and that 575,000,000, with 15,000,000 each, had reportedly been approved, and sought NIA's assurance.

thread.speaker: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez
thread.said: Rodriguez reported that NIA's regional director had followed the administrator's instruction and asked for confirmation that the consolidated district projects were approved. The agency-side response was recorded as 'Yes, sir.'

thread.speaker: Rep. Romeo Momo Sr.
thread.said: Momo said his district's two national irrigation systems served thousands of hectares but that a 5,000,000 allocation for repair, maintenance, and upkeep was insufficient. He asked how NIA allocated its limited budget and urged equitable, rather than equal, distribution toward major rice-producing areas.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA said its first priority was ongoing projects and that savings could be used for modifications. The official committed to provide Momo a list of modifications for the year.

thread.speaker: Rep. Reynolds Michael Tan
thread.said: Tan questioned declining NIA funding for Region 8, citing 2,100,000,000 for 2025 and 1.61149000000000 1,000,000 billion and 149,000,000 for 2026 as spoken. He said Region 8 had submitted 8,000,000,000 but only 149,000,000 was approved and requested the reason.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA attributed the reduction to the gap between its almost 250,000,000,000 request and the 46,000,000,000 available, with tier-one ongoing projects receiving priority. The official said modifications could be considered for shovel-ready projects but remained subject to approval and restrictive special provisions.

thread.speaker: Rep. Reynolds Michael Tan
thread.said: Tan requested a province-by-province copy of the FY 2027 NIA allocation and clarification on what funds could be modified from FY 2026. NIA said restrictions made modifications difficult and reiterated its request for greater flexibility.

thread.speaker: Rep. Nelson Legacion
thread.said: Legacion asked NIA to clarify the FY 2026 irrigation budget and sought a proportional adjustment for validated projects in his district. He cited projects totaling 990,000,000 and said the district allocation was only 12,000,000, as spoken.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: NIA stated that its FY 2027 proposal was 235,000,000,000 and that the district allocation was 1,021,000,900, while 93,000,000 was listed for the relevant district and 990,000,000 appeared associated with projects outside it. The figures and geographic attribution were not fully clear in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Minority representative Soberi
thread.said: Soberi asked NIA to clarify Bukidnon Third District allocations, citing an RDC-endorsed 2,025,772,000,000 for an earlier period, 273,000,000 for 02/2027, and zero for Bukidnon Third District. She requested a discussion and updated figure.

thread.speaker: NIA official
thread.said: The agency said the figures were based on provincial agriculture proposals and indicated that an update would be provided. No definitive revised Bukidnon allocation was stated on the record.

topic: Rice production support and fertilizer assistance
summary: Members raised agricultural damage, rice production support, fertilizer procurement, irrigation, mechanization, and high-value-crops funding. The DA cited National Rice Program support of about 26.4 billion, projected 2026 rice production of about 19 million tons, and possible imports of up to 5 million tons because of El Niño. The agency said inorganic fertilizer assistance for 2027 would primarily use a QR-code voucher system and requested 8.73 billion for fertilizer. Officials also sought higher funding for farm-to-market roads, post-harvest facilities, and high-value crops, while the committee manifested support for tripling the road request and confirmed a 20% Mindanao share. The DA committed to provide equipment and seed-program details, review the seed proposal for funding, and complete geofencing by year-end.
question: The committee sought to establish whether the proposed FY 2027 budget would adequately support rice production, fertilizer access, irrigation, mechanization, post-harvest capacity, and high-value crops. Members also pressed the DA on projected rice imports and the measures intended to reduce import dependence.
agency_position: The DA said rice supply through 2026 was expected to be secure but that El Niño could lower production and require precautionary imports of up to 5,000,000 tons. It supported expanded irrigation, mechanization, seed development, QR-code fertilizer vouchers, post-harvest investment, high-value-crops funding, and geofencing, while agency officials requested additional funding and several officials undertook to provide details or review proposals.
outcome: The DA answered the committee's principal questions on rice targets, projected imports, fertilizer vouchers, and planned production measures, but several funding requests remained proposals rather than final appropriations. The agency committed to submit or review supporting details, including the seed-system breakdown and mechanization concerns, and to pursue geofencing.

positions.position: Supported geofencing but argued that it needed to be accompanied by stricter land-use-conversion rules and stronger protection for prime agricultural land.
Pressed for adequate National Rice Program production support, fertilizer assistance, and funding to repair and protect an irrigation siphon.
Questioned the scale and durability of rice imports and sought a permanent production-based solution to import dependence.
Opposed relying solely on lowest-bid procurement when it resulted in unreliable agricultural machinery and supported farmer choice through a fertilizer voucher system.
Pressed for a 20% Mindanao share, supported higher farm-to-market-road and post-harvest funding, and backed the QR-code fertilizer voucher system.

They cited 2,500,000,000 pesos in agricultural damage, P1.14 billion in 2024 damage and losses, 6,700,000,000 for El Niño preparation, and a 2027 assistance package of about 10 billion. outcome: The agency answered the broad design of disaster assistance and identified a 2027 package of about 10,000,000,000, but the hog-raiser indemnification request remained dependent on DBM approval and possible supplemental funding. Agricultural-land impacts, the detailed production plan, and several garbled production figures were not fully resolved and were referred for submissions or later consultation.

positions.position: Flood recovery, farmer welfare, food security, and agricultural resilience were major budget priorities, particularly because flooding had affected a key rice-producing area.

Hog raisers required prompt indemnification or other assistance, and the unresolved claims and production concerns warranted a concrete agency plan. Abaca production also needed stronger market and industrial support.
The geofencing proposal was a positive step but needed to be accompanied by stricter land-use-conversion rules and stronger protection for prime agricultural lands.

topic: Climate resilience, flood mitigation, and post-harvest loss reduction
summary: Vice Chair Anna York and other members framed flooding, climate risk, food security, and post-harvest losses as central budget concerns. The DA said climate shocks had caused around 114 billion in agricultural damage and losses between 2024 and 2026, while irrigation coverage remained incomplete and post-harvest infrastructure and cold storage had significant gaps. Officials cited 6.7 billion for El Niño-related fuel and transport subsidies, about 10 billion for the 2027 assistance package, and an additional 10 billion being considered for climate-resilient DA facilities. NIA explained that irrigation projects were prioritized using weighted technical, economic, fiscal, regulatory, geographic, and drought-related criteria. Members also sought action on flood mitigation, sedimentation, dam capacity, the Ifugao rice terraces, and rubber-gate replacement. The agencies committed to submit documents and complete geofencing by year-end, but several project-specific issues remained unresolved or unclear.
question: The committee sought to establish how the DA and NIA would use the FY 2027 budget to protect agriculture from flooding, climate shocks, irrigation shortfalls, and post-harvest losses. Members also asked whether the agencies had sufficient fiscal space, how irrigation and flood-control projects were prioritized, and what measures would be taken to preserve vulnerable production areas and facilities.
agency_position: The DA and NIA said climate resilience required expanded irrigation, resilient facilities, improved storage and processing, post-harvest machinery, cold-chain infrastructure, flood and sedimentation controls, and targeted assistance after calamities. The agencies maintained that projects were prioritized through technical, economic, regulatory, geographic, drought-related, and fiscal-space criteria, but several specific project-status and rubber-gate questions remained unclear.
outcome: The agencies presented climate resilience, irrigation expansion, post-harvest infrastructure, cold storage, disaster assistance, and sedimentation control as budget priorities. The DA committed to submit geofencing-related materials and complete the program by year-end, while NIA committed to submit irrigation-project information; the flood-mitigation status, expropriation concern, heritage-site prioritization, and rubber-gate replacement schedule were not clearly resolved.

positions.position: Flood recovery, food security, farmer welfare, and climate resilience should be central considerations in approving the FY 2027 DA and NIA budgets.
The DA's fiscal space was inadequate relative to climate and infrastructure needs, and irrigation projects required disciplined prioritization and transparency.
Irrigation funding should prioritize the restoration and preservation of the Ifugao rice terraces and the agency should resolve the raised expropriation and flood-mitigation concerns.
NIA needed to account for dam capacity, sedimentation, flood-control functions, and the durability and timely replacement of rubber gates.

topic: Animal-industry competitiveness, ASF, vaccines, and pork imports
summary: Allan Ty asked how the DA would use the animal competitiveness allocation and whether it would comply with RA 12308 and use livestock tariff collections as the revenue source. The DA said full use of 20,000,000,000 would effectively begin in 2028, while a 2027 framework would support herd buildup, repopulation, dairy, and related programs; it undertook to submit an amendment. DA officials cited current livestock tariff collections of about 22 billion annually, including 11,100,000,000 certified collections, and said a tariff classification change could yield 4,000,000,000, peso in additional revenue. Members also sought anti-rabies data, an animal-industry intervention breakdown, and responses to ASF and low hog prices. Secretary Laurel attributed farm-gate pressure to ASF, cited declining pork imports in some categories, opposed continuous importation subject to WTO constraints, and supported ASF vaccine deployment and livestock repopulation. Nicanor Briones requested vaccine funding, border biosecurity facilities, and reference-value import valuation, with the DA undertaking to coordinate with DBM and implement the valuation request.
question: The committee sought to establish how the DA would use the animal competitiveness allocation, finance animal-health and production interventions, address ASF and low hog prices, and manage pork imports and biosecurity. Members also asked whether the DA would provide vaccines, strengthen border inspection, and revise import valuation and tariff practices.
agency_position: The DA said the ANCEP allocation would support herd buildup, repopulation, dairy, vaccine manufacturing, and related animal-industry interventions, but that full implementation would effectively begin in 2028 because of organizational and administrative requirements. It opposed continuous pork importation, cited WTO constraints, supported ASF and AI vaccine capacity, and undertook to work with DBM and the Tariff Commission on funding, tariffs, classifications, biosecurity, and import valuation.
outcome: The DA answered the principal questions but left several matters dependent on amendments, DBM coordination, Tariff Commission work, and requested data submissions. Support for hog raisers and vaccine funding was expressed, but the implementation details and final funding decisions remained open.

thread.said: The administrator said the CEDA program was preallocated by law, so reducing the allocation from 2,000,000,000 to 1,000,000,000 cut implementation by 50%. The effects were across the board, including infrastructure, block-farm programs, and scholarships.

thread.speaker: Minority member Siberi
thread.said: Siberi confirmed that the cuts affected programs across the board and said the reduction was especially concerning because of El Niño and RSSI. She then asked for the status of the SRA presidential assistance for farmers program.

thread.speaker: SRA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said releases under the presidential assistance program were ongoing. The total for the industry was 420 something million, mostly from DSWD, and almost 100,000,000 had been released.

thread.speaker: Minority member Siberi
thread.said: Siberi asked how much of the released assistance had been allocated to Bukidnon.

thread.speaker: SRA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said he did not know the percentage allocated to Bukidnon at that time and would provide the information.

thread.speaker: Minority member Siberi
thread.said: Siberi said Bukidnon was one of the country's largest sugar-producing areas and expressed concern over the expansion of affected areas, citing a latest calculation of 576 hectares in three months. She asked the DA Region 10 representative about a request to expand the regional laboratory budget for biological control and related RSSI response.

thread.speaker: DA Region 10 director
thread.said: The director said the region initially had capacity to treat five hectares per day, increasing to 20 hectares when infection reached 1.1 percent and to 30 hectares after discussions with the SRA in Bukidnon. The region could supply biological control for up to 30 hectares per day and planned to reach 100 hectares per day before the end of the year.

thread.speaker: DA Region 10 director
thread.said: The director said the infection rate had been around 0.87 percent per month since January. He said the planned 100-hectare-per-day capacity would be more than enough for the existing 2.2 percent infection affecting sugarcane out of 45,000 hectares.

thread.speaker: DA Region 10 director
thread.said: The director said the DA had proposed more or less 150,000,000 under a quick response plan to expand laboratory capacity and prevent infection from reaching 5 percent. He said the DA had classified infection into low, moderate, and severe levels to guide the response.

thread.speaker: Minority member Siberi
thread.said: Siberi asked the director to confirm how far capacity would be increased before year-end, noting that the affected area had reached 576 hectares in three months and could rise to 1,000 or even 2,000 hectares within another one to two months.

thread.speaker: DA Region 10 director
thread.said: The director said Crystal Milling Corporation had been helped to establish its own laboratory. He said a farmers' group had initially needed 20 hectares per day, but the capacity had increased to 30, and private-sector laboratory participation could help keep infection below 5 percent.

thread.speaker: Minority member Siberi
thread.said: Siberi asked how much funding the DA Region 10 needed to reach the expanded response capacity.

thread.speaker: DA Region 10 official
thread.said: The official identified 150,000,000 as the amount submitted under the quick response plan.

thread.speaker: DA Region 10 official
thread.said: The official said the 45,000 hectares of sugarcane represented more than a billion in value and explained that capacity was being increased to avoid exceeding a 5% infection rate.

thread.speaker: Minority member Siberi
thread.said: Siberi said the requested funding was not even 10% of the value generated in Bukidnon and characterized it as a small investment with potentially large returns. She urged the Secretary to support funding for both DA laboratory capacity and a higher SRA budget.

thread.speaker: Minority member Siberi
thread.said: Siberi returned to the SRA's procurement bottleneck and asked whether new acquisition procedures had delayed implementation.

thread.speaker: SRA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said new rules, including rules referred to as "MARB and stuff like that," had delayed procurement. He said the SRA was making up for the delay during the last quarter of the year.

thread.speaker: Minority member Siberi
thread.said: Siberi welcomed the response and said she supported not only maintaining but increasing DA funding and working toward stronger agricultural production.

topic: Post-harvest facilities, food hubs, ice plants, and cold storage
summary: The DA described a network of food hubs, processing centers, and mega cold storage facilities, including projects associated with Benguet State University and Clark. A minority member questioned large Benguet farm-to-market-road allocations and requested coordinates and project reports to verify that the roads were needed and not duplicative. DA officials said annual post-harvest losses were 250 billion and identified around 6.5 billion for 2027 post-harvest funding, while the High Value Crops Development Program requested an 8 billion increase from its current 1.7 billion budget. Rep. Rufus Rodriguez supported larger infrastructure funding, and an agency official requested a 50% increase in post-harvest support. Rep. Romeo Momo Sr. sought support for a 739 million Abaca Agro-Industrial Corridor in Marihatag, including 47 million for 2027, and confirmed that a proposed Lianga facility was an ice plant and cold storage. The DA undertook to check coordinates, provide reports, and endeavor to advance the Marihatag project, but no final funding approval was recorded.
question: What funding, projects, and implementation details did the DA and attached agencies have for post-harvest facilities, food hubs, ice plants, and cold storage? The committee also sought to establish whether proposed facilities and supporting roads were adequately funded, properly located, and integrated with production and marketing areas.
agency_position: The DA said post-harvest losses were substantial and that a national network of dryers, food hubs, processing centers, mega cold storage facilities, and supporting farm-to-market roads was needed to stabilize supply, quality, and prices. DA officials sought increased funding, including around 6,500,000,000 for post-harvest facilities and an 8,000,000,000 increase for the High Value Crops Development Program, and confirmed that the Lianga proposal involved an ice plant and cold storage facility.
outcome: The committee received the DA's rationale for expanding post-harvest, food-hub, processing, and cold-storage infrastructure and heard requests for higher funding. The DA committed to provide or verify supporting farm-to-market-road documentation, while the Benguet, Lianga, and Marihatag proposals remained subject to funding and implementation decisions.

topic: Mindanao and regional equity in DA and NIA allocations
summary: Rep. Rufus Rodriguez pressed the DA to raise Mindanao's share to 20%, citing Mindanao's contribution to food production, while DA officials sought additional FMR, post-harvest, fertilizer, and high-value-crops funding. The FMR infrastructure request included about 30 billion for an additional 2,000 kilometers, while post-harvest funding was cited at about 6.5 billion, fertilizer at about 8.73 billion, and the requested high-value-crops increase at about 8 billion over a current 1.7 billion budget. Rep. Reynolds Michael Tan questioned unreleased FMR funds, road standards, and declining Region 8 NIA allocations, and requested province- and project-level breakdowns. Rep. Nelson Legacion challenged FMR reductions and sought proportionate irrigation funding and hatchery support; the DA said its regional director would act on the hatchery concerns. A minority member requested a regional seed-system breakdown, and Secretary Laurel said the DA would review it and commit to funding it. Minority member Soberi linked Bukidnon's output of about 36.09 billion to the need for NIA support, but the apparent district allocation discrepancy remained unresolved while NIA undertook to update the figures.
question: The committee sought to establish whether DA and NIA allocations for Mindanao, regions, provinces, and congressional districts were proportionate to agricultural output, irrigable land, validated projects, and implementation needs. Members also asked whether FMR, irrigation, post-harvest, fertilizer, high-value-crops, seed-system, and hatchery funding should be increased or reallocated.
agency_position: The DA and NIA said allocations were constrained by available funds, cash flow, priority Tier 1 and ongoing projects, and restrictive special provisions. DA officials nevertheless supported increased or integrated funding for FMRs, post-harvest facilities, fertilizer, high-value crops, and seed-system interventions, while NIA indicated that greater budget flexibility and project-level review were needed.
outcome: The hearing produced support for higher and more flexible regional and program funding, but did not settle the conflicting FMR, Region 8, district irrigation, or Bukidnon figures. The agency undertook to provide or update certain project-level information and to pursue hatchery and seed-system follow-up.

positions.position: Mindanao should receive a 20% share of DA funding because of its major contribution to national food production, and FMR, post-harvest, fertilizer, and high-value-crops funding should be increased.
Region 8's declining NIA allocation required explanation, province-level itemization, and possible adjustment; DA and DPWH FMR standards should also be harmonized.
FMR reductions and insufficient irrigation allocations were inconsistent with validated district projects and farmer needs; he sought proportionate funding and support for legislated hatcheries.
The seed system program required a detailed regional intervention breakdown and possible additional funding.
Bukidnon's leading agricultural output warranted continued DA and NIA support and clarification of the apparent zero or reduced district allocation.

topic: Land-use conversion, geofencing, and agricultural-land protection
summary: Members raised concerns about the PacSilica development, industrial projects, marshland conversion, and solar installations on irrigable or rice land. The DA cited about 1,600 directly affected farmers in the Clark area but said the full agricultural impact had not yet been established. The DA supported geofencing of key crop lands, with 3 million hectares of rice land identified as needed and an 8% slope threshold discussed for land-use decisions. The secretary committed to complete geofencing by the end of this year and to undertake studies on industrial impacts and marshlands, with possible marshland implementation in mid-2027 subject to World Bank support. The DA also said solar-powered pumps could involve 100 megawatts, potential income of 600,000,000, and a proposed rate of 4 pesos per kilowatt hour, but said the agricultural effects of solar use on flat rice land still required research. A minority member additionally requested a breakdown of the 34,000,000 seed system program budget, which the secretary agreed to review.
question: The committee sought to establish how the DA would protect agricultural and irrigable land from conversion, industrial development, and solar projects, including through geofencing and impact studies. Members also asked what studies, implementation timelines, and program-level interventions would be provided for 2027.
agency_position: The DA supported geofencing to reserve prime agricultural and irrigable areas for food production, using crop, slope, soil, water, and moisture-retention characteristics. It acknowledged that studies on industrial developments, marshlands, and solar use on rice land were incomplete, while undertaking to complete or advance several studies and to finish geofencing by the end of this year.
outcome: The DA undertook to submit geofencing materials, complete geofencing by the end of this year, and produce or advance studies on industrial impacts, marshlands, and solar use on agricultural land. The compatibility of solar projects with flat rice land and the full PacSilica agricultural impact remained unresolved, while implementation of the marshland study was contingent on funding and possible World Bank support.

positions.position: Geofencing was a step in the right direction but needed to be accompanied by stricter land-use-conversion rules and stronger protection for prime agricultural land.
Industrial development should be subject to DA studies covering land reclassification, irrigation and hydrologic effects, contamination risks, and impacts on smallholder farmers and cooperatives.
Irrigable land should be protected from conversion to solar subdivisions, and marshland studies and a clear 2027 implementation timetable were needed.
The DA should provide a detailed regional and project-level breakdown of the seed system program's interventions.

topic: National irrigation systems, maintenance, and infrastructure rehabilitation
summary: DA Undersecretary Asis Perez reported that about 2.2 million hectares of an estimated 3.13 million irrigable hectares had been served, while the DA had added about 21,400 hectares and restored about 3,600 hectares through small-scale irrigation and canal works. Representative Juju Cesar Bergara sought action on an irrigation siphon, for which an agency official cited a request for 45,000,000 and a 194.5-meter length. Representative Marlo Bancoro pressed for multi-year irrigation and solar-irrigation implementation; the agency cited a 2027 proposal of about 1.12 billion but only 29,000,000 for the relevant item because of fiscal limits. Members also urged marshland studies, preservation of the Ifugao rice terraces through irrigation, and investigation of stalled solar projects. NIA reported a dam capacity of 54,000,000 cubic meters and discussed rubber-gate lifespans ranging from 15 to 45 years, but the replacement schedule was unclear. Representative Romeo Momo argued that the 5,000,000 NIA maintenance allocation for his district was inadequate, and NIA committed to provide a list of budget modifications or savings.
question: The committee was trying to establish whether irrigation systems, canals, dams, siphons, gates, and solar-irrigation facilities were adequately funded and maintained for 2027. Members also sought to determine which rehabilitation and expansion projects would be prioritized, and whether the agencies would provide studies, revised allocations, or implementation timelines.
agency_position: The agencies said irrigation expansion, canal rehabilitation, dam and gate maintenance, and solar-irrigation projects were necessary but constrained by limited fiscal space. NIA stated that ongoing projects were prioritized and indicated that it would provide additional allocation information, while DA officials committed to coordination, studies, and follow-up discussions on delayed or proposed projects.
outcome: The hearing established that irrigation maintenance and expansion needs exceeded available allocations, particularly for siphon repair, solar irrigation, dam and gate maintenance, and NIA upkeep. The agencies gave several follow-up commitments, but the precise rubber-gate timetable, the adequacy and revision of district maintenance allocations, and several project funding decisions remained open.

A minority representative requested marshland studies and a timetable for implementation, and the DA said the study would be completed by year-end with implementation potentially beginning in mid 2027. topic: NIA appropriation structure and congressional oversight
summary: Allan Ty questioned the NIA administrator on whether irrigation appropriations should be program-based or rigidly itemized, and whether program-based budgeting still subjected projects to DBM validation, procurement laws, auditing, engineering standards, and congressional oversight. NIA answered that it preferred program-based appropriations supported by a separately submitted and validated project list, because itemization in 2026 had limited its ability to respond to cost changes, rights-of-way problems, calamities, and implementation delays. Robert Nazal Jr. separately questioned the DA's farm-to-market road funding, noting a 55,050-kilometer deficit, a reduction from about 33 billion in 2026 to about 16 billion in 2027, and a stated 51.5% cut. Secretary Laurel said roughly 60 billion annually could build about 4,000 kilometers, with the minimum effort taking ten to twelve years, and said DA had allocated 30% of its 33 billion budget based on absorptive capacity and manpower. Nassal also asked whether special provision number eight had constrained NIA utilization and requested a written proposal before plenary. The issue landed with NIA's requested program-based structure still subject to committee consideration, supported by document submissions, while the answer on whether cuts would leave projects functionally incomplete remained unclear.
question: The committee sought to establish whether NIA's irrigation appropriations should remain program-based or be itemized by project, and whether either structure preserved DBM validation, procurement and audit compliance, implementation flexibility, and congressional oversight. It also examined whether budget restrictions affected NIA's utilization and whether DA had the capacity to implement the proposed farm-to-market road funding.
agency_position: NIA preferred restoring program-based appropriations under program expenditure classification, with a detailed, validated, and transparent project list submitted separately to DBM and Congress. It maintained that this structure preserved accountability and oversight while allowing adjustments for field conditions, delays, calamities, savings, and implementation readiness.
outcome: NIA's preferred program-based structure was placed on the record, with separate project-list documentation for validation and oversight. The committee requested the Speaker-submitted request and a written implementation proposal; the effect of project cuts on functional completion was not answered clearly.

positions.position: Supported determining whether program-based appropriations could preserve validation, accountability, transparency, and congressional oversight while avoiding the implementation constraints of rigid project line items.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked the NIA administrator to confirm that NIA was a government-owned and controlled corporation receiving national government subsidies for development, construction, and rehabilitation of the national irrigation system.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator confirmed that NIA was a government-owned and controlled corporation and received national government subsidies for the national irrigation system.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked how NIA expanded, appropriated, and utilized its annual national government subsidy.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said NIA evaluated priorities, explained its prioritization, and identified the budget in a program-expenditure form. The phrase describing the form was garbled in the transcript.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked whether, in fiscal year 2025 and prior years, NIA's budget was presented under program expenditure classification rather than as an extensive list of individual irrigation projects in the NEP or GAA.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator confirmed that the budget was presented under the program-based structure.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator clarified that NIA submitted a detailed project list as a supporting document, but individual projects were generally not separate line items in the NEP or GAA annex.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked whether NIA was still required under the program-based framework to submit its proposed project list and supporting documents to DBM for technical evaluation, validation, and budget review.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said NIA submitted the project list and supporting documents to DBM. Projects underwent technical validation, prioritization, costing, and assessment of implementation readiness; their absence as individual GAA line items did not mean they were unvalidated or that NIA had unlimited discretion.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked whether the program-based appropriations remained subject to DBM evaluation, procurement laws, auditing rules, engineering standards, and congressional oversight.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator agreed, stating that a program-based budget did not remove accountability. Projects remained subject to DBM evaluation, procurement and auditing requirements, approved engineering plans and specifications, environmental and other regulatory requirements, and monitoring and reporting to Congress.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said NIA had written to the Speaker requesting more flexibility, while emphasizing that the flexibility was operational rather than discretion without accountability.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked what operational challenges resulted from itemizing individual NIA projects in fiscal year 2026, particularly in relation to project costs, rights-of-way, emergencies, and calamities.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said that making projects separate budget line items created significant operational difficulties. Changes in detailed engineering, project scope and cost, right-of-way problems, permits, calamities, or other irrigation requirements could require reprioritization, but funds could not readily be redirected to other validated and implementation-ready projects without a lengthy modification or realignment process.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked whether the list submitted to DBM was for planning and validation, subject to final costing and implementation-readiness assessment, rather than a rigid statutory enumeration of projects.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator agreed, explaining that under the previous program-based structure NIA could proceed with another validated, high-priority, implementation-ready project within the same program when a project encountered an unavoidable delay.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked whether NIA had recommended the dated list of individual projects to DBM or whether DBM had imposed it.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said NIA submitted the list during budget preparation, but it should be treated as a planning, prioritization, and validation document. NIA supported submitting a complete and validated project list while recommending that the appropriations remain program-based.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked which structure would better serve farmers: a rigid itemized project list in the GAA annex or program-based appropriations supported by a separately submitted, validated, and transparent project list.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator preferred restoring the program-based structure. He said it would provide operational flexibility to address delays, use legitimate savings, respond to calamities and emerging irrigation needs, and prioritize validated projects ready for implementation without compromising congressional oversight or project-level transparency.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked whether NIA had submitted, or was submitting, a request to amend its budget from an itemized list to a program- or subprogram-based structure.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator confirmed the request and reiterated that the detailed project list should be submitted as a supporting document for transparency, validation, monitoring, and oversight rather than as rigid line items.

thread.speaker: Allan Ty
thread.said: Allan Ty asked NIA to submit to the committee the request it had sent to the Office of the Speaker.

thread.speaker: Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Robert Nazal Jr. noted that DA identified a 55,050 kilometer farm-to-market road deficit and that proposed 2027 funding would fall from 33,000,000,000 in 2026 to 16,000,000,000, a 51.5% cut.

thread.speaker: Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal asked Secretary Laurel whether building around 1,000 kilometers annually was too little to materially reduce the deficit and improve agricultural productivity, production costs, post-harvest losses, market access, and farmer incomes.

thread.speaker: Laurel
thread.said: Secretary Laurel agreed that the level was insufficient and described the criteria used to prioritize roads, including influence area, poverty incidence, farmer or fisherfolk beneficiaries, network connectivity, road condition, climate adaptation, average daily traffic, and new production areas.

thread.speaker: Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal asked how much would ideally be needed annually for farm-to-market roads and how many kilometers that funding could build.

thread.speaker: Laurel
thread.said: Laurel estimated that 60,000,000,000 annually might be needed and said this could build about 4,000 kilometers, described as a bare minimum over ten to twelve years.

thread.speaker: Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal asked whether DA could demonstrate lower-cost construction than DPWH in terms of absorptive capacity and whether it had enough manpower.

thread.speaker: Laurel
thread.said: Laurel said DA had a 33,000,000,000 budget that year and had allocated 30% in consideration of its absorptive capacity and manpower. He said DA would be more ready the following year.

thread.speaker: Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal asked the NIA administrator whether the more specific itemization of projects in fiscal year 2026 and the addition of special provision number eight improved implementation or contributed to the decline in budget utilization.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator said NIA preferred program-based operations under program expenditure classification, supported by a detailed, validated, and transparent project list submitted separately to Congress and DBM. He said this provided a balance between transparency, accountability, oversight, flexibility, and timely utilization, while not granting unlimited authority to replace projects.

thread.speaker: Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal followed up on whether special provision number eight had limited NIA's room to implement projects and affected utilization.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator cited the difficulty of rigid line items, using a 100-meter irrigation canal with a transcript figure stated as 10,000,005 million as an example. He also said delays in early procurement affected implementation and contrasted NIA's constraints with DPWH's ability to implement projects at any time of year.

thread.speaker: Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal asked NIA to submit a proposal to the committee, before plenary, identifying provisions that would improve implementation.

thread.speaker: Robert Nazal Jr.
thread.said: Nassal asked whether a substantially reduced appropriation for a designed and costed irrigation project could still deliver its intended functional output or would result in an incomplete project.

thread.speaker: NIA administrator
thread.said: The administrator began responding, but the answer was interrupted and is not intelligible in the transcript.
